key_terms.meaning: Energy stored in an elastic body by the work its own deformation absorbs; for a linear spring U = ½P Δ, units joule (J)
U = P²L/(2AE) for a bar of force P, length L, area A, modulus E
U = ∫ M²/(2EI) dx over the beam length; EI is flexural rigidity
U = T²L/(2GJ) for constant torque T, shear modulus G, polar second moment J
δ = ∂U/∂P: partial derivative of strain energy with respect to a load gives displacement at that load along that load
A fictitious load Q applied at a point where no real load acts, so that ∂U/∂Q gives the deflection there; set Q = 0 after differentiating
External virtual work equals internal virtual work: 1·Δ = Σ (n·δL) for any self-consistent virtual force system
Truss deflection Δ = Σ (n N L)/(AE), where N is real member force and n is member force from a 1 kN load at the point
For a plane truss, m + r − 2j; m members, r reaction components, j joints; zero means determinate
A member beyond the minimum needed for stability; its force cannot be found from joint equilibrium alone
Solve each joint in turn using ΣFx = 0 and ΣFy = 0; start at a joint with at most two unknown member forces
Δ = ∫ Mm/(EI) dx, with M real bending moment and m moment due to a unit load at the point and direction wanted
An equation stating that a displacement at a released point must equal a known value, usually zero when a support is restored
The extra reaction removed to make the structure determinate; its value is then found from compatibility
M₁L₁ + 2M₂(L₁+L₂) + M₃L₂ = −6A₁x̄₁/L₁ − 6A₂x̄₂/L₂ for constant EI; A is area of the free bending moment diagram, x̄ its centroid distance
Bending moment at a support of a fully clamped span under given load; it is the starting value in moment distribution
DF = k/Σk at a joint, where k = I/L is member stiffness; shares the unbalanced moment among the members meeting there
Fraction of a distributed moment carried to the far end of the same member: ½ if the far end is fixed, 0 if it is pinned

takeaways: A linear elastic member stores exactly half the work you put into it, so U = ½PΔ for any loading type.
Each loading type has one closed form: P²L/(2AE) for axial, ∫M²/(2EI)dx for bending, T²L/(2GJ) for torsion.
Castigliano turns a derivative of energy into a deflection, which removes the need to integrate slopes directly.
The unit load method is Castigliano rewritten as internal work, and it needs only two force analyses of the same structure.
For a truss the unit load integral collapses to a simple sum over members: Σ nNL/(AE).
For a beam the same idea becomes ∫Mm/(EI)dx, one integral with two bending moment diagrams.
Indeterminacy is not a dead end: remove a redundant, compute the gap by energy, then force the gap to close.
Clapeyron's equation handles one span pair at a time, while moment distribution handles one joint at a time; both end in simultaneous or iterative solutions for support moments.
bank_note: Long answers are expected to derive the energy expression from first principles, then apply it to a truss or beam with a clear, labelled force or moment diagram and consistent units.

bank.q: Define strain energy for a linearly elastic body. Derive the expression for strain energy stored in a uniform bar under axial load, and show that it equals half the product of load and extension.
outline: Define U as work done by gradually applied load, U = ½PΔ
Use Δ = PL/(AE) and substitute
Obtain U = P²L/(2AE), state units joule
Explain why the factor ½ appears (load grows from 0 to P)
Mention energy is always positive and is recovered on unloading

bank.q: State Castigliano's theorem for displacement of a linear elastic structure. Explain the condition under which it is valid and how a dummy load is used to find deflection at a point with no load.
outline: State δ = ∂U/∂P, displacement along the line of action of P
State linear elasticity and constant temperature requirement
Explain total U in terms of all loads, differentiate with respect to one
Describe dummy load Q, differentiate, then set Q = 0
One worked one-line example of a cantilever tip deflection

bank.q: State the principle of virtual work for deformable bodies and use it to derive the unit load formula for deflection of a pin-jointed truss.
outline: Virtual force system in equilibrium, real displacement field compatible
External virtual work = 1 × Δ
Internal virtual work = Σ n·δL with δL = NL/(AE)
Equate and obtain Δ = Σ nNL/(AE)
Define n and N clearly and note sign convention for tension

bank.q: Explain the method of joints for a plane truss. Define the degree of static indeterminacy m + r − 2j and explain what happens when it exceeds zero.
outline: Assumptions: pin joints, loads at joints, members two-force
Two equilibrium equations per joint
Condition m + r = 2j for determinacy
Definition of m, r, j with a simple example
Excess members are redundant; compatibility needed

bank.q: A cantilever beam of length L and constant EI carries a point load W at the free end. Using the unit load method, find the deflection and slope at the free end.
outline: Write M(x) = −W(L−x) from the free end
Apply unit vertical load at tip, write m(x)
Integrate ∫Mm/(EI)dx between 0 and L
Result WL³/(3EI) downward
For slope apply unit moment and obtain WL²/(2EI)

bank.q: A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load w per unit length. Find the central deflection by the unit load method.
outline: Support reactions wL/2 each
M(x) written for both halves or by symmetry
Unit load at midspan gives m(x) triangular diagram
Integrate 2∫₀^(L/2) Mm/(EI)dx
Result 5wL⁴/(384EI)

bank.q: A pin-jointed steel truss of m members and j joints carries given joint loads. Explain step by step how you would compute the vertical deflection of a chosen joint by the unit load method, including a tabular layout.
outline: Check determinacy m + r = 2j
Find all N by method of joints
Apply 1 kN at the chosen joint in the wanted direction, find all n
Table with L, A, E, N, n, nNL/(AE) per member
Sum with consistent units and state direction of deflection

bank.q: A propped cantilever of span L with constant EI carries a UDL w over the whole span. Using the redundant reaction method with energy, find the prop reaction and the fixing moment.
outline: Release the prop, treat it as redundant R
Deflection at prop due to UDL = wL⁴/(8EI)
Deflection due to R = RL³/(3EI)
Compatibility: wL⁴/(8EI) − RL³/(3EI) = 0 giving R = 3wL/8
Fixing moment 8wL²/... check by statics: M = wL²/8 at fixed end

bank.q: A continuous beam has two equal spans L, each carrying a UDL w, with the ends simply supported. Apply Clapeyron's three-moment equation to find the support moments.
outline: State three-moment equation with A and x̄ for UDL
End moments zero at simple supports
Symmetry gives M₁ = M₃ = 0, solve for M₂
Free bending moment diagram parabola, A = (2/3)wL³/... use 2wL³/... values
Answer M₂ = −wL²/8

bank.q: A continuous beam of two spans, 6 m and 4 m, with constant EI, carries a central point load on each span. Solve for the support moments by moment distribution and sketch the bending moment diagram.
outline: Compute stiffness k = I/L for each span, distribution factors
Fixed end moments from standard table
Unbalanced moment at the interior joint, release and distribute
Carry over half to far fixed ends, sum iterations
Final moments, reactions, bending moment diagram with values

bank.q: A hollow circular shaft is loaded in torsion and a bracket attached to it is loaded in bending. Write the total strain energy of the assembly and use Castigliano's theorem to find the deflection at the bracket tip.
outline: Separate energy terms: torsion T²L/(2GJ), bending ∫M²/(2EI)dx
Note axial term if present
Add terms to get total U in terms of P at tip
Differentiate ∂U/∂P
State that each term contributes independently

bank.q: Compare Castigliano's theorem and the unit load method for finding deflections. Show that one follows from the other, and discuss when each is more convenient.
outline: Both require linear elasticity
Differentiate total energy with respect to real load versus internal work of unit load
Show unit load result equals ∂U/∂P when differentiation and integration are interchanged
Castigliano needs no separate force analysis for statically determinate structures
Unit load is easier for many load cases and for indeterminate structures

bank.q: A continuous beam over three spans is to be analysed. Compare the three-moment equation and the moment distribution method for accuracy, effort and suitability for hand calculation, and state clearly which you would choose for four spans or more.
outline: Three-moment gives simultaneous equations, exact, effort grows as number of supports
Moment distribution is iterative, converges quickly for usual stiffness ratios
Both give same final support moments for constant EI
Three-moment needs EI constant or span-wise ratios; moment distribution handles variable EI naturally
Recommendation with reason and note on checking by statics

bank.q: A truss has one redundant member. Explain how you would find its force using strain energy and compatibility, and evaluate how the choice of which member to call redundant affects the work done.
outline: Degree of indeterminacy m + r − 2j
Cut redundant, treat its force X as unknown load on determinate structure
Member forces N = N₀ + X·n, energy U(X)
Compatibility ∂U/∂X = 0 because the gap must close
Different redundant choices give identical final forces but different arithmetic

glossary.def: Energy absorbed by a body as it deforms elastically, recoverable on unloading.
The area above the load-deflection curve, equal to strain energy for a linear elastic material.
The product EI, resisting bending of a beam.
The product GJ, resisting twist of a shaft.
The product AE, resisting axial stretch of a bar.
Work done by a virtual force system moving through real displacements, or the reverse.
A load of magnitude one applied in the direction of the displacement being sought.
Plot of bending moment along a member, used inside the energy integrals.
Moment in a span as if it were simply supported, used with the three-moment equation.
Moment developed at a clamped support of a single span under a given load.
Structure whose support reactions and member forces follow from equilibrium alone.
Structure with more unknowns than equilibrium equations, requiring compatibility.
Condition that displacements at a point must match the restraints actually present.
An extra reaction or member force that is removed to make the structure determinate.
For linear elastic structures, effects of separate loads add directly.
Member loaded only at its ends by pins, so its force acts along its axis.
Truss member carrying no force under the given load case, identified at a joint by inspection.
Pin connection where truss members meet and where equilibrium is written.
The ratio I/L used in moment distribution to measure a member's share of moment.
Fraction of an unbalanced joint moment assigned to one member.
Moment induced at the far end of a member when the near end is rotated.
Lateral joint translation in a frame or truss that adds extra unknowns.
Bending moment at a continuous beam support, negative for hogging.
A load applied at a point, as opposed to a distributed load.
